correctness.rationale: Four mutually exclusive pair configurations are completely classified: equality, proper ancestry in either direction, incomparability. Every realized atomic triple type is listed, with necessary and sufficient conditions. Quantification over possible second points reduces to intervals of ancestor gaps, descendant gaps or branch distances with tests capped at three. This proves the rank-three upper bound at all heights. Explicit rank-three height and binary-branching separators prove the converse. The two pair-profile implementations matched 7,098 parameter instances, and independent actual-vertex C++ triple enumeration confirmed all stated small test cases; tests are not substituted for the infinite argument.

value.rationale: Natural complete rank-three classification of the full two-parameter family of uniform finite rooted trees in its minimal ancestry-only reduct. Exact smallest representatives and distinct sharp saturation thresholds for height and branching are structural expressibility results, with direct use for distinguishing ancestry queries and controlling finite logical representatives. Not just a finite table, a restatement of known general bounds, or a cosmetic invariant.
